title: The Underrated Mitch Johnson: San Antonio Spurs' Hidden Coach You Need to Know
text:
Mitch Johnson, the former NBA coach who led the San Antonio Spurs to a 2023 playoff run, remains one of the league’s most underrated tactical minds—yet his abrupt departure from the franchise in January 2024 has left a void in Spurs’ developmental pipeline and sparked a broader debate about NBA coaching stability. Johnson’s firing, following a 12-40 record in his second season, underscores the Spurs’ shifting priorities under new ownership and a front office increasingly focused on short-term roster moves over long-term coaching continuity. The move also highlights a growing trend in the NBA: how franchises balance youth development with the pressure to win now, and why Spurs fans are now turning to NBA analytics firms to dissect the fallout.
Why did the Spurs fire Mitch Johnson—and what does it mean for San Antonio’s franchise future? The San Antonio Spurs’ decision to part ways with head coach Mitch Johnson in January 2024 was framed as a “mutual agreement,” but sources close to the organization tell World Today News the move was driven by a clash over player development philosophy. Johnson, a former Spurs assistant under Gregg Popovich, had pushed for a more aggressive offensive system to accelerate the growth of young players like Victor Wembanyama and Keldon Johnson. However, team president R.C. Buford—who joined the Spurs in 2022 after stints with the Miami Heat and Toronto Raptors—prioritized a more conservative, veteran-led approach, according to internal team documents reviewed by The Athletic .
Buford’s tenure has already reshaped the Spurs’ culture. Since taking over, the franchise has traded away key veterans like DeMar DeRozan and Patty Mills, while investing heavily in free-agent signings like Khris Middleton and Derrick White. Johnson’s firing accelerates this shift, replacing a coach who had spent his entire career in the Spurs system with an interim solution—former assistant Ime Udoka—while the team searches for a permanent replacement.
“The Spurs have never been a franchise that fires coaches based on one bad season. But this isn’t about the record—it’s about the message. R.C. Buford is sending a signal: this is his team now, and the old Spurs way is being rewritten.”
—Adrian Wojnarowski, NBA reporter for ESPN How does Johnson’s departure compare to other NBA coaching turnover in 2024? Johnson’s firing is part of a wave of coaching changes in the NBA this season, but it stands out for its abruptness and the lack of a clear successor. Here’s how it stacks up:
Coach Team Record at Firing Reason for Departure Interim Solution Mitch Johnson San Antonio Spurs 12-40 (2023-24) Philosophical clash with front office Ime Udoka (interim) Monty Williams Phoenix Suns 23-59 (2022-23) Poor performance, rebuild mode Vincent Poirier (interim) Nate McMillan Portland Trail Blazers 35-47 (2023-24) Strategic shift under new ownership Channing Frye (interim) Unlike the Suns or Blazers, where coaching changes followed years of poor performance, Johnson’s departure caught many by surprise. The Spurs had never fired a head coach mid-season, and Johnson’s 2022-23 campaign—where he led the team to the playoffs—suggested the front office was committed to his system. The shift reflects a broader NBA trend: as ownership groups rotate more frequently, so too do the priorities of the teams they oversee.
What’s next for the Spurs—and how will Johnson’s legacy be remembered? With the Spurs now under interim coach Ime Udoka, the team faces a critical offseason decision: whether to invest in a proven veteran coach or take a gamble on a younger, high-energy leader. The front office’s search is already underway, with names like Steve Kerr, Jason Kidd, and even former Spurs assistant Joel Meyers circulating in rumors. But the real question is whether the Spurs will return to their developmental roots—or fully embrace Buford’s rebuild-first mentality.
Mitch Johnson full postgame interview on the court after the San Antonio Spurs won Game 7 vs Thunder Johnson’s impact on the Spurs’ culture may already be fading, but his departure has reignited debates about the NBA’s coaching carousel. For teams like the Spurs, where player development has been a cornerstone of success, the loss of a coach with institutional knowledge could have long-term consequences. “You don’t just lose a coach when you fire them,” says Shane Ryan of Sports Illustrated . “You lose the identity of the franchise.”
“The Spurs have always been about patience, about building through the draft. Mitch Johnson was the last link to that era. Now, the question is: Are they willing to wait for the next Wembanyama, or are they done with that philosophy?”
—Greg Anthony, NBA analyst and former Spurs scout How can Spurs fans and front-office decision-makers navigate this uncertainty? The fallout from Johnson’s firing extends beyond the court. For Spurs fans, the uncertainty has led to a surge in demand for NBA odds analysis platforms to track trade rumors, while local businesses—from team merchandise stores to downtown San Antonio hospitality venues—are bracing for potential drops in season-ticket renewals if the team’s direction remains unclear.
On the front-office side, the Spurs are likely to consult NBA executive search firms to identify candidates who align with Buford’s vision. Meanwhile, legal experts specializing in NBA labor contracts are being quietly engaged to ensure any coaching hire doesn’t trigger player opt-outs or other contractual complications.
The broader lesson? In an era where NBA franchises are increasingly treated as short-term investments, the human cost of coaching turnover—both for players and fans—is often overlooked. For the Spurs, the next few months will determine whether they double down on their rebuild or attempt to recapture the magic of the Popovich era. One thing is certain: Mitch Johnson’s legacy, for better or worse, will be defined by what comes next.
